items.title: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces
items.summary: Foundation models, now powering most of the exciting applications in deep learning, are almost universally based on the Transformer architecture and its core attention module. We identify that a key weakness of such models is their inability to perform content-based reasoning, and make several improvements: letting SSM parameters be functions of the input, and designing a hardware-aware parallel algorithm in recurrent mode.

items.title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
items.summary: High throughput serving of large language models requires batching sufficiently many requests at a time. However, existing systems struggle because the KV cache memory for each request is huge and grows and shrinks dynamically. We propose PagedAttention, an attention algorithm inspired by virtual memory and paging, and build vLLM on top of it.

items.title: FlashAttention-3: Fast and Accurate Attention with Asynchrony and Low-precision
items.summary: Attention, as a core layer of the ubiquitous Transformer architecture, is the bottleneck for large language models and long-context applications. FlashAttention-3 exploits asynchrony of tensor cores and TMA, interleaves block-wise matmul and softmax, and uses block quantization with FP8 for low-precision attention.

items.title: Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding
items.summary: Inference from large autoregressive models like Transformers is slow - decoding K tokens takes K serial runs of the model. We introduce speculative decoding - an algorithm to sample from autoregressive models faster without any changes to the outputs, by computing several tokens in parallel.

items.title: Mixtral of Experts
items.summary: We introduce Mixtral 8x7B, a Sparse Mixture of Experts (SMoE) language model. Mixtral has the same architecture as Mistral 7B, with the difference that each layer is composed of 8 feedforward blocks. For every token, at each layer, a router network selects two experts to process the current state and combine their outputs.

items.title: RWKV: Reinventing RNNs for the Transformer Era
items.summary: Transformers have revolutionized almost all natural language processing tasks but suffer from memory and computational complexity that scales quadratically with sequence length. RWKV combines the efficient parallelizable training of transformers with the efficient inference of RNNs.

items.title: Quantum error correction below the surface code threshold
items.summary: Quantum error correction provides a path to reach practical quantum computing by combining multiple physical qubits into a logical qubit, where the logical error rate is suppressed exponentially as more qubits are added. We present a surface code memory operating below threshold on a superconducting processor.

items.title: A Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm
items.summary: We introduce a quantum algorithm that produces approximate solutions for combinatorial optimization problems. The algorithm depends on a positive integer p and the quality of the approximation improves as p is increased.

items.title: A variational eigenvalue solver on a photonic quantum processor
items.summary: Quantum computers promise to efficiently solve important problems that are intractable on a conventional computer. We present the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE), a hybrid approach that uses a quantum processor to prepare trial states and a classical optimizer to find the ground-state energy.
